I am 63 years old and have worked this land for 40 years. My wife and I, just two of us now, eight mu of land. I will plant maize on most of it and keep some for mungbean like always.

For the maize, I plant Zhengdan hybrid seed — the dealer in town sells it, my neighbor Old Wang has been using it three years and gets good ears. I buy about 2 kg seed for each mu. I plow the field once with the tractor before planting, 80 yuan per mu for the tractor man, then I sow in early April when the ground is warm enough.

Fertilizer is the big cost. I use the compound fertilizer, the one with three numbers on the bag — I put two bags per mu before planting, that is about 100 jin, 50 kg. Then when the maize is knee-high I put urea, one bag covers about two mu, so half a bag per mu, that is maybe 25 jin of urea. If the leaves look yellow I add a little more urea at tasseling. Better to put a bit extra than have small ears — a bad harvest hurts much more than wasting some fertilizer money.

Water from the well — I irrigate maize maybe three times: after planting if the rain does not come, at the big trumpet stage, and when the grain is filling. Electricity for the pump costs money but maize without water gives nothing.

Pesticide — I spray once for the borer worm when I see the holes in leaves, and once more if armyworm comes. Two sprayings usually enough. My neighbor sprays three times but I think that is too much money.

For mungbean, I keep one mu. Mungbean does not need much — it is tough. I use my own saved seed from last year, improved type I bought two years back. No plowing, I just use rotary tiller light pass. I put half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, no urea — mungbean makes its own nitrogen, everyone knows this. One irrigation if dry, one spray for aphids. Mungbean gives me money for household because price is good in market.

Last year maize gave me about 550 kg per mu, mungbean about 120 kg per mu. This year I expect similar if weather is normal.
